answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity stake that cannot be shared. To join, an agent locks a bond refundable only on clean exit, and duplicates funded by one controller are traced through deposit provenance, so the registry treats them as one actor and every address must post its own slashable stake. Even a small delta in detected duplication destroys the swarm's margin. A juniper of forged keys collapses into a single payer, so faking a whole mesa of agents means one bond per address plus fees, all forfeitable on detection.
